notes: ⭐ THE COMMONS IS THE GAME (Dean, 09/09/2026, docs/commons-handoff-2026-09-09-v1.md, rules C1-C10). THE FIVE NOTICE BOARDS SIT IN THE CENTRE OF THE TABLE, all five whatever suits are in play, and nobody owns one: a farm is a Farmstead and a Barn. THE TURN IS (1) ONE BONUS, then (2) ONE CORE ACTION - bonusTiming 'start', and that order is Dean's reversal of the 03/09/2026 ruling, on the grounds that a turn visibly ends on the main action. THE BONUS IS: play any ONE card from your hand onto one central board and take that board's action - wheat Harvest, vegetable Deliver, orchard Draw 2, apiary GROW, dairy Build - with the fee EXTRA in every case and no colour matching. A board whose action you cannot legally perform right now is not offered, which is the standing ruling unchanged. HARVEST takes one of your full buildings OR the whole pile from any central board holding at least one card, into your barn, including a board you played on this turn (C5: a good turn, not a loop). THERE ARE NO MEEPLES ANYWHERE (C6) - no starting supply, no meeple on the island's 3 VP space, no spend, no Collect - and the tile's 6 VP / 3 VP split stands alone. WHY: the meeple visit failed at the table, in Dean's words, because "with a meeple always available the bonus was basically free". NO NUMBER FROM ANY reference-v14 OR EARLIER REPORT IS COMPARABLE.

THE TWO GAMES THE COMMONS REPLACED ARE CONTROLS AND THEIR CODE IS NOT DEAD. overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json is the v31 card visit of 02-04/09/2026; overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json is the v1 meeple loop of 04/09/2026; overlays/meeple-economy-v1.overlay.json is the meeple ECONOMY of 05/09/2026, which is the reference-v14 game and the last rules a report quotes. THE STANDING RULE THAT KEEPS THEM: a branch whose only producer is a knob at its shipped value is NOT deleted. ⚠️ AND THE 05/09/2026 LESSON THAT COST THIS PROJECT A RULING: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to PIN every knob the flip moved, so each of those three now pins visitCurrency, bonusTiming, startingMeeplesPerColour and the Orchard door's draw beside whatever it was already pinning. Name the passengers before ruling an arm in, not after.

commonsThreshold AND commonsColourMatch ARE THE TWO FALLBACK KNOBS AND BOTH SHIP OFF (C10, Dean 09/09/2026). They exist so that if the bonus reads AUTOMATIC at the table - and it might, because playing a card is always available where a meeple visit at least needed a meeple - the cap is one number away rather than a design pass away. commonsThreshold (null = no cap) refuses a play onto a central board already holding that many cards, which is the only thing in the commons that would ever refuse a play, so turning it on is a real change to C4 and not a tuning. commonsColourMatch (false) demands the card played match the board's suit, with two cards of any suits as a wild pair at the island's substitution rate. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES THEM IS DEAN'S BAND: the bonus should be taken on 30% to 60% of turns. Above 60% at two players, commonsThreshold is the next run. overlays/commons-threshold-2.overlay.json and overlays/commons-colour-match-v1.overlay.json are the arms.

⭐ THE TWO HARVEST KNOBS OF THE CENTRE, BOTH SHIPPED OFF (Dean, 09/09/2026). His question, in his own words: "Can we measure how many cards are taken when the Harvest is done against the centre cards? I'm interested to see if we place a threshold on the centre cards if it will reduce the number of cards going from the centre to the barns - my target is about 30-40% of barn cards should come from the middle." The centre share read 63.1% on the shipped rules. commonsThreshold was the first answer and it MEASURED NO CHANGE at 2 (63.1% against 63.0%), for two reasons that are the whole of why these two exist: a central harvest already takes a median of only 2 cards, so a cap of 2 caps almost nothing; and every card played onto the centre reaches SOMEBODY'S barn eventually unless the game ends first, so capping the INFLOW cannot reduce the OUTFLOW, it can only slow it. commonsHarvestMin (null = the shipped C5 rule, any non-empty pile) is the BUILDING semantic: a pile is "full" at n and may not be harvested below it. commonsHarvestTake (null = the whole pile, C5) is the only one of the three that can reduce the centre's outflow WITHOUT reducing plays, because the cards it leaves behind stay in the centre. ⚠️ READ ALL THREE AGAINST THE CONSERVATION LINE a18 now prints: plays into the centre = cards harvested out + cards stranded at game end. A knob that moves the share by stranding cards has changed where the cards END UP, not how the centre feeds a barn during play. overlays/commons-harvest-min-2, -3, -4 and overlays/commons-take-1, -2 are the arms, with overlays/commons-threshold-1, -2 and -3 beside them.

THE ORCHARD DOOR IS DRAW 2 AND THAT IS A CHOICE, NOT AN INHERITANCE (Dean, 09/09/2026). workers.roster.draw.draw is 2/2 in the shipped data, where it was 3/3 for the whole life of the card visit. The self-cancellation law that made it 3 - a door priced in its own output currency has to over-deliver against the free Draw 1 - died with the free Draw 1 on 04/09/2026 and has no subject here either. ⚠️ BUT THE COMMONS PUTS A FEE BACK ON THE BONUS: a play costs a card, so a Draw 2 door returns 2 for 1 and nets +1, which is thinner than any other door's return. Whether that leaves the Orchard board dead is the one contested door number in the game and overlays/commons-draw-three.overlay.json is the arm. The v31 control pins 3/3 because that game measured with it.

THE APIARY BOARD IS A GROW, NOT A SOW (C3). It is the one door whose ACTION changed with the commons, and it is carried in the data as workers.roster.sow.actionUnderCommons - a SECOND printed payload beside `action`, exactly as drawUnderMeepleCurrency sits beside `draw`, so that the two controls keep their Sow door without having to pin a leaf. Pay the building's activation card into its stack as normal and gain the ability; the fee for the board is extra, and there is NO clog bypass - that was the meeple-paid Grow of R15 and it went with the meeples.

The numbers that belong to no single card: setup quantities, the turn's shape, the one standing economy rate and the end-game trigger. Anything PRINTED on a card lives in cards.json instead, anything printed on the island lives in island.json, and the five door actions live in workers.json.

SCHEMA VERSION 2 IS v31 (Dean, 02/09/2026, docs/design-changes-v31-2026-09-02-v1.md). The bump is not cosmetic: the file lost seven keys in one edit and every one of them was a coin. If you are reading a v31 number against a report written before 02/09/2026, stop - the reference was re-cut as reference-v10 and no historical number in reports/ is comparable.

THERE ARE NO COINS. Not zero coins: no coin. Nothing is earned in them, nothing is priced in them, there is no coin tie-break and there is no coin knob. What went with the currency, in one list so nobody re-derives it from an old doc: startingCoins, upgradeCostCoins (there are no starter upgrades at all now), coinPityDivisor, visitPayout in all four of its branches, giftDiscardCoins, buyCost (the card buy) and marketCost (buy at market). Six of those seven were already null or already deleted in spirit by 19/08/2026; the seventh, the upgrade price, went with the upgraded faces. The design reason is the standing finding the market note used to carry, taken all the way: money is what buys SOLITAIRE in this game, because a visit is bought with a card and every other bonus option was bought with a coin, so a coin sink in the bonus slot crowds the visit out all game. Deleting the currency deletes the competitor. The 30 Power and Endgame cards now cost 2 cards of their OWN suit, and card text that read GBP 2 or GBP 1 reads Draw 1.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: THE PARAGRAPH BELOW DESCRIBES THE MEEPLE GAME AND IS HISTORY. The shipped turn is the COMMONS turn in the note above it - bonus FIRST, a card onto one of five central Notice Boards, no meeple anywhere. What follows is kept because it is the record of the game overlays/meeple-economy-v1.overlay.json and overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json reproduce, and because the code that runs it is not dead: those two arms are the only things exercising it. THE TURN, in the order it is played (the meeple loop, Dean 04/09/2026): (1) ONE core action - Draw, Build, Grow, Harvest, Deliver; (2) ONE bonus option, either VISIT (place one meeple from your supply in the colour slot of a NEIGHBOUR'S Notice Board and immediately perform that colour's plain action) or COLLECT (take every meeple off your own Notice Board into your supply, then Draw 1). WHAT THIS DELETED FROM v31, and none of it is dormant - it is gated off and reachable only through overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json: the turn-start meeple phase (spend any number of meeples, one at a time, each leaving the game for good), the standalone free Draw 1, the card fee on a visit, and the self-visit. A meeple is now spent in the bonus slot and only there, one a turn, and a spent meeple is never removed from the game - it moves onto the neighbour's board and comes home to them on their Collect. That is the loop the design is named for, and it is also the denial: while it sits there, that colour of that neighbour is shut to the whole table. THE WILD SPEND: any TWO meeples from your supply may be spent as one of any colour, both landing in the slot bought.

baseDraw IS 2 SEE, 2 KEEP - the plain Draw action keeps BOTH cards and discards nothing. It was 2-see-1-keep from v13 until v31. The reason for the change is not generosity, it is that the discard was the last piece of hidden bookkeeping in the core five actions and it bought nothing measurable; the game's clock is now the card supply and the end trigger, not a per-draw tax. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH THE BONUS SLOT, which changed on 04/09/2026 and changed in the game's favour: the standalone free Draw 1 is gone, so the only card the bonus slot can buy is the one attached to COLLECT. A seat taking Draw as its action and Collect as its bonus still nets 3 cards a turn with no interaction at all - collecting an EMPTY board is legal and reads as a bare Draw 1 - so the solitaire line survived the deletion with a haircut rather than a burial. Measured: it took 54.2% of turns against the v31 free Draw 1's 67.6%. That is the shape action inflation shows up in first, and it is the number the bonus mix has to keep counting separately from a Collect that actually took meeples back.

⭐ 09/09/2026, AND READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY HAND NUMBER: 7 IS THE SIMULATOR'S BOUND, NOT A GAME RULE (C7). The table plays with NO hand limit and Dean found that positive. The simulator cannot enumerate an end-of-turn discard without a bound - the paragraph below is what happened the one time it tried - so the engine keeps 7 and EVERY REPORT HEADER MUST SAY SO. A bot-side discard heuristic in place of the rule is what a future session needs before it can measure the table's hand, and nobody has designed one. THE HAND LIMIT IS BACK, AT A FLAT 7 (12 on the day it was reinstated, cut to 7 the same day for runtime), AND IT IS A GAME RULE RATHER THAN A CARD VALUE (Dean, 02/09/2026, reversing one v31 change on evidence). WHAT THE DELETION MEASURED, because this is the number that decided it: v31 removed the limit and the first simulator run after it found the deletion had quietly removed the bound on the LEGAL-MOVE ENUMERATOR as well. The comment over `subsets` in packages/engine/src/actions.ts read 'hands are 6-8', and that bound WAS the hand limit - nothing else in the game was holding it. With hands reaching 34 cards a 2-seat position offered 43,879 legal moves, 43,845 of them build payments, because C(33,4) is 40,920 ways to pay for ONE buildable card; a re-measurement on 02/09/2026 at n=4 games found a worse position still at 116,535. A 2-seat game went from about 0.1 seconds to 1-15 minutes, so the watch-list suite could only be run at n=8 and every conclusion from that run is an anecdote. The bots hoarded to a median hand of 18, the free bonus Draw 1 became strictly dominant (beating a neighbour visit 3:1, failing the hook assertion) and the 2-seat game ran to 45 rounds. IT IS A DESIGN FAILURE BEFORE IT IS AN ENGINEERING ONE: a gateway player choosing between forty thousand ways to pay for one build is not a shippable turn, and diminishing returns on a card in hand are what make a neighbour worth visiting at all. THE SHAPE OF THE RESTORED RULE IS NOT THE OLD ONE. It is ONE GLOBAL NUMBER, not five printed per-suit ones - the Barn still prints nothing and stays blank, because this belongs on the player aid where a rule that applies to everybody belongs. It is checked at the END of your turn only; you may exceed it mid-turn, which is how several cards work (O14 sows a whole hand, W10 empties one into the barn) and is the old rule kept deliberately. Overflow discards down to the limit at the turn boundary. 12 IS A GUESS AND A KNOB: it is roughly three turns of accumulation above the 4-card opening hand, generous enough that the limit is a brake rather than a clock, and overlays/hand-limit-10.overlay.json and overlays/hand-limit-15.overlay.json are the paired arms, and overlays/hand-limit.sweep.json is the full ladder. null disables the rule and restores the v31 behaviour, which is the control arm nobody should run without reading the numbers above first.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: STILL CLOSED, AND NOW CLOSED TWICE OVER. Under the commons the bonus slot holds ONE option - play a card onto a central board - so there is no Collect for this number to size and no free draw of any kind (C9). The value stays 1 and is read only by the two controls. bonusDraw IS NO LONGER A BONUS OPTION OF ITS OWN (04/09/2026). The number survives and is read in one place only: it is how many cards COLLECT draws after sweeping your board. Under overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json it goes back to being the standalone free Draw 1, taken instead of visiting a Notice Board, and the yardstick every door had to beat - which is what made the Orchard door a Draw 3 rather than a Draw 2 under those rules, because a door handing back 2 cards for the 1 card you placed was worth exactly the free option. THAT WHOLE ARGUMENT HAS NO SUBJECT UNDER THE SHIPPED RULES: a visit costs no card, so there is nothing to cancel, and the free option is gone, so there is nothing to be worse than. The Orchard door is a plain Draw 2 and the door set has no exception left in it. Raising this number is still the cheapest way to make the solitaire line beat every door in the game at once, and it is the lever Dean declined to sweep on 03/09/2026; it now carries a meeple sweep with it, so it is no longer a pure solitaire dial.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: STILL DEAD, AND NOW FOR A SECOND REASON. Nobody owns a central board, so there is no such thing as visiting yourself and nothing for the flag to permit (C1, C9). It stays true in the data and is read only by the v31 control. selfVisitAllowed IS DEAD UNDER THE SHIPPED RULES AND IS READ ONLY BY THE CONTROL. It was risk 2 of the v31 pass, armed on purpose: you could place your bonus card on your OWN Notice Board and take your own suit's action, with the only brake being that your card counted toward your own threshold and shut your own door. IT MEASURED AT ABOUT 22% OF TURNS and the meeple loop deletes it outright (rule X5: there is no self-visit under any flag, and the enumerator refuses one whatever this key says). The risk it named did not go away, it changed defendant: the free Draw 1 ate the slot, not the self-visit, and the empty-board COLLECT is what inherited the job. a08-the-hook must still count a self-visit separately and must still never credit one as interaction - under the shipped rules it should assert the line reads exactly 0, which is a claim worth failing on rather than an assumption. Set true or false as you like here; only overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json makes it mean anything.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: REVERSED. bonusTiming IS 'start' AGAIN (Dean, C2): the bonus is taken FIRST and the turn visibly ends on the main action. 'end' - the 03/09/2026 correction described below - is now the paired control at overlays/commons-bonus-last.overlay.json. Read the two paragraphs together and do not quote either ruling without the other: this is a reversal on Dean's own call, not a drift. bonusTiming (Dean, 03/09/2026 - A CORRECTION, NOT AN EXPERIMENT): the turn is meeples, then your CORE ACTION, then the bonus option. This engine and both design docs had carried the opposite order since 19/08/2026 ('start': bonus before the action) and were simply wrong about the game. 'start' survives as the paired control (overlays/bonus-first.overlay.json) and 'any' as v14's once-per-turn-any-point (overlays/bonus-any-time.overlay.json). THE THREE ARE NOT ORDERABLE BY POWER: under 'start' a door can fuel the action that follows it, under 'end' the action can set the door up - fill a building then Harvest it through the Wheat door, harvest into the barn then Deliver through the Vegetable one - so expect the DOOR MIX to move and not only the visit rate. SLOT UNSPENT still reads the window, but its absolute is the rational floor and only the delta between arms means anything.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: SUPERSEDED. visitCurrency IS 'commons'. The meeple visit failed at the table - Dean: "with a meeple always available the bonus was basically free" - and 'meeple' is now a CONTROL at overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json (the v1 loop) and overlays/meeple-economy-v1.overlay.json (the reference-v14 game). Everything below is the record of why it was ruled in, and it is still true of those arms. visitCurrency IS meeple AND THAT IS THE GAME (Dean ruled it in 04/09/2026; docs/meeple-loop-visit-handoff-2026-09-04-v1.md is the design, docs/meeple-loop-measurement-2026-09-04-v1.md is what it measured). A visit costs a MEEPLE placed in the colour slot of a NEIGHBOUR's Notice Board, never your own; the Notice Board is not a building at all - no threshold, no stack, no sow, no harvest, no clog - and the bonus slot's other half is COLLECT. card is the v31 game and is now the CONTROL, at overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json: a card fee onto a board that is a building with a threshold of 2, self-visiting legal, a standalone free Draw 1, the turn-start meeple spend, the Orchard door at Draw 3 and a meeple on both delivery spaces of every tile. WHAT meeple IGNORES: selfVisitAllowed and economy.noticeBoardThreshold. bonusTiming, bonusSlotsPerTurn and handLimit all still apply and are unchanged. IT WAS RULED IN ON A MEASUREMENT THAT WAS NOT FLATTERING, and pretending otherwise would make the next reader mistrust this file. The hook FELL, 0.41 to 0.37 rival visits per player per turn, and the game got 35-43% LONGER. It was ruled in on the two things that did move: the two dead meeple colours came back to life (Apiary and Dairy take 46% of door uses against 32%, and the door-mix assertion goes FAIL to PASS), self-visiting became impossible by construction, and interaction per GAME rose 21% even as interaction per turn fell. Whether the hook is a per-turn or a per-game quantity is a design decision nobody has made. NO NUMBER FROM BEFORE THIS IS COMPARABLE: the reference is re-cut as reference-v12.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: BOTH ARE SUBJECTLESS UNDER THE COMMONS. startingMeeplesPerColour ships at 0 and meepleCapPerColour at null because there are no meeples in the shipped game at all (C6). Both are read only by the meeple controls, which pin their own values. The paragraph below is the record of what they measured while they were the game. startingMeeplesPerColour AND meepleCapPerColour ARE THE ECONOMY'S TWO NUMBERS, and both are read only under visitCurrency meeple (rules R3 and R4). Every player starts with ONE meeple of each of the five colours, NOT drawn from the island bag, so the loop is primed before anybody delivers and a first-turn visit is possible at every seat. THE STARTING FIVE ARE THE IGNITION, NOT AN ACCELERANT: the arm with none reads a hook of 0.09 and an empty-board Collect on 87% of turns, which is the solitaire draw engine v31 already was, only slower. ⭐ THERE IS NO CAP. meepleCapPerColour IS null (Dean, 05/09/2026: "let's just remove the cap completely - there is no limit to how many or what colour meeple you can hold"), so nothing a seat gains is ever refused and the only things that remove a meeple from the game are the two tolls. ⛔ THAT IS THREE RULINGS IN TWO DAYS AND THE MIDDLE ONE WAS AN ACCIDENT, so the history is written out here rather than left to be re-derived. 04/09: Dean ruled the cap at ONE, deliberately against its own sweep, on teach simplicity - "you may never hold two of a colour" is a rule a player checks at a glance. 04/09 evening: the amended R4 set it to 2 inside the handoff v2 arm, as a processing bound. 05/09 morning: R17 was ruled in AS MEASURED and the 2 shipped with it, a passenger nobody argued for. 05/09, once that was pointed out: Dean removed the cap outright. ⭐ WHAT REMOVING IT MEASURED, paired at n=4820 (reports/watchlist-2026-09-05T15-14-10-reference-v13-meeple-no-cap-v1.txt): the bonus mix crossed the line, rival visit 31.3% against the empty-board Collect's 31.1%, so assertion 17 goes FAIL to PASS and the verdict reads 2 PASS / 3 FAIL / 8 OBSERVE; the hook, the door mix, the barn glut, actions per turn and game length ALL HELD; and the suite got FASTER, 220.3s against 266.7s. ⚠️ READ THE PASS HONESTLY: 31.3 against 31.1 is a gap of 0.2 points and reference-v13 has no noise floor, so the slot is LEVEL and the assertion has landed on the near side of level. It is not a win over the solitaire line. ⭐ AND THE ANTI-PILE FEAR IS MEASURED AND DEAD: with no cap at all, the largest supply any seat ever reached across twelve 4-seat games was NINE meeples in total and never more than THREE of one colour, and the median supply in the last third is still 1.0. The cap of two was sitting just above what players actually accumulate, which is why removing it changed so little. THE COMPONENT COUNT IS NOW DETERMINISTIC AND IS DEAN'S QUESTION, NOT THE ENGINE'S: nothing is destroyed but tolls, so the meeples in circulation are five per player plus one per tile - 32 at four seats - against a printed bag of 25 (C54).

⚠️ 09/09/2026: SUBJECTLESS UNDER THE COMMONS and shipped false. Read only under visitCurrency 'meeple', which is now a control. Kept in full because overlays/meeple-economy-v1.overlay.json turns it back on and because the finding it carries - a currency that leaves the game is a drain however good the reason for spending it - outlives the rule. meepleAsCard IS R15 (Dean, 04/09/2026 evening, docs/meeple-loop-visit-handoff-2026-09-04-v2.md), AND SINCE 05/09/2026 IT DEFAULTS true: it is the shipped game. Wherever a rule asks you to pay or spend a card, a meeple of the matching colour may pay it instead - build costs including the n-of-suit requirements and the 'any' slots, the 2-own-suit cost on Power and Endgame cards, a Grow's activation payment, and a delivery crate. It is NOT a Sow, because a Sow is a placement and a meeple is not a card to place, and it is NOT a balloon move cost (C62, a default rather than a ruling). R10's wild pair is reused rather than re-rated: two meeples of any colours are one card of any colour, at the same rate they are one meeple of any colour. A meeple never counts toward the hand limit, because it is never in a hand. A meeple paid into a Grow never joins the stack and never counts toward the threshold, so IT CAN ACTIVATE A BUILDING ALREADY AT ITS THRESHOLD - a priced clog bypass, Dean's ruling of 04/09/2026, and the one thing R15 does that a card never could. ⭐ WHERE THE MEEPLE GOES IS NOT THIS KNOB, IT IS meepleAsCardGoesTo, AND UNDER R15 ALONE THE ANSWER WAS THE BOX AND THAT KILLED THE LOOP: see the R17 note below. false is the v1 loop of 04/09/2026, where a meeple only ever performs its colour's action through a neighbour's board and is never a payment; it survives as overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json, which is now a real arm again rather than the no-op it was for a day.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: SUBJECTLESS UNDER THE COMMONS and shipped null. A central board has no slots and no threshold, so nothing in the commons is ever priced or refused (C4). Read only by the meeple controls. slotToll IS THE AMENDED R6 (Dean, 04/09/2026 evening), AND SINCE 05/09/2026 IT DEFAULTS 1: A NOTICE BOARD SLOT IS PRICED, NOT BLOCKED. Nothing is ever refused. Visiting a slot that already holds k meeples costs 1 times k EXTRA meeples of ANY colours on top of the acting meeple, and every one of those extra meeples - the toll - goes STRAIGHT TO THE BOX, never to the host. So a slot already holding two meeples costs three to visit: one joins the slot as normal, two are boxed. A wild pair sitting in a slot counts as two occupants, not one. ⚠️ THE TOLL IS A SINK, NOT A PAYMENT TO THE HOST. Dean's own framing is that it 'might be a good way of sinking surplus meeples' under the amended cap of 2, so read it beside meepleCapPerColour and never alone, and read it beside paymentSlotToll, which is the SEPARATE and FLAT toll a payment placement pays. Under R17 the toll is the main drain left: 57.5% of the 12.16 meeples leaving the game each game is toll. null is the v1 rule - a slot holding any meeple is BLOCKED and refuses that colour outright until the owner Collects - and it survives in overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json and in the v31 control.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: ALL THREE ARE SUBJECTLESS UNDER THE COMMONS. They are left at their 05/09/2026 values ('board', 1, 'perPayment') rather than nulled, so that overlays/meeple-economy-v1.overlay.json reproduces the reference-v14 game by pinning visitCurrency and meepleAsCard alone. ⭐ meepleAsCardGoesTo, paymentSlotToll AND paymentHostChoice ARE R17 (Dean, 05/09/2026), THE CHANGE THAT MADE THE MEEPLE ECONOMY A LOOP RATHER THAN A DRAIN, AND THE REASON THIS FILE'S DEFAULTS MOVED. Read all three only under meepleAsCard true. A meeple spent as a card is PLACED ON ANOTHER PLAYER'S NOTICE BOARD, in its own colour's slot, exactly as a visit places one, and the host takes it back on their Collect. ⛔ IT BUYS THE PAYER NOTHING ELSE: no door action, it is not a visit, and the bonus slot is untouched. The WHOLE payment goes to ONE chosen host (paymentHostChoice perPayment; perMeeple was Dean's first ruling the same day and was ruled back on the branching factor, 25,827 ways to buy one building at four seats against 4,063). Landing on a slot that already holds a meeple costs ONE FLAT extra meeple of any colour, to the box, however deep the slot (paymentSlotToll 1), and that flatness is the one place it differs from slotToll. WHY IT EXISTS: under 'box' the resource use ATE the loop - meeples left the game 18.27 times a game against 9.44 visits, median supply in the last third hit 0.0, and the hook collapsed 0.35 to 0.09. Placing them instead recovered the hook to 0.31 and produced the closest thing to a level bonus slot this project has measured: rival visit 30.9% of turns against the largest solitaire line's 31.9%, a gap of ONE point where every previous version sat 21 to 75 points apart. It also SHORTENED the game (3p 35.4 to 26.5 rounds). ⚠️ IT WAS RULED IN WITH THREE COSTS ON THE TABLE, recorded here so nobody reads the flip as free: 2-player blocked-want tripled 1.2% to 7.7% (C65, which reopens C57 and Dean's island alternative X2), the barn glut DOUBLED +0.5 to +1.0 and is the first movement in that number across four arms (C66), and the balance suite runs 2.6x slower. 'box' is the handoff v2 arm and survives as overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json, which is now the control for R17.

SETUP IS FOUR CARDS AND NOTHING ELSE. startingHand is 4 from your own suit deck, startingBarnCards is 0, and there are no coins to start with. The barn starts EMPTY, which is new: it used to be seeded with 1 card. The barn is now purely a place to store cards ready for delivery and PRINTS NOTHING - and that survives the hand limit coming back, because the limit is no longer a card value. See turn.handLimit below.

⚠️ 09/09/2026: STILL READ ONLY BY THE v31 CONTROL. A central board has NO threshold under the commons - any number of cards, never full, never clogged (C4) - so clog as a denial tool has no subject in the shipped game for the second version running. noticeBoardThreshold IS READ ONLY BY THE v31 CONTROL (04/09/2026). Under the shipped rules the Notice Board is not a building: query.thresholdOf returns null for it, which makes isFull false, canTakeCard false and roomOn 0, so it falls out of the sow targets, the harvest targets, the Apiary door's legality check and A21 The Wax Hall's count all at once, and nothing can ever be placed on it. What blocks a door now is a MEEPLE IN A SLOT, one colour at a time, cleared by the owner's Collect rather than by a Harvest - and it measured far gentler than the old clog: the blocked-want rate at 2 players is 1.3%, and no seat ever had all five slots blocked, at any seat count. THE HISTORY IS WORTH KEEPING because it is the only lever ever measured to move the suit balance, and it was monotone across three paired n=1580 arms on the older two-building surface: at t=4 Orchard won 80.8%, at t=3 62.8%, at t=2 42.0% against an even share of 36.4%. On the later single-door surface at n=500: t=5 clogged 2.3% of turn boundaries, t=3 5%, t=2 11%, with the suit spread most even at 2. Dean's reading of why a loose door is worse than it looks: 'you get to use other players cards a lot, but that number also decreases how often you can harvest and make use of the cards people give you, making it more valuable to the visitor rather than the person who is visited.' Never raise it without re-running the suite against the control, which is the only arm it now moves.

endGame.trigger is deliveryCount (Dean, 2026-08-09, with the flat island) and survives v31 untouched in its wording and at risk in its number. The game ends when any ONE seat completes its deliveriesToTrigger-th ISLAND delivery, after which every other player takes furtherTurnsEach more turns. Balloon moves are Deliver actions but not island deliveries, so they never count. It is still one observable trigger read off public state - a receipt count in front of a player - and still a thing a player does rather than a deck running out. It is FLAT at every seat count, so 6 is half the 2-seat island's 12 delivery spaces, a third of the 3-seat island's 18 and a quarter of the 4-seat island's 24; that asymmetry is known and taken, and 2p is where to watch it. WHY IT IS NOW THE FIRST KNOB TO SWEEP, AND THE REASON HAS REVERSED. v31's forecast was a SHORTER game: the bonus slot bought a whole core action for one card and meeples added uncapped free ones. Measured, it ran LONGER, and the meeple loop then added 35-43% on top of that (2p 32.8 rounds, 3p 31.6, 4p 30.3 against 27.6 / 23.4 / 21.2). Actions per turn FELL, 2.39 to 2.21, while turns rose - the arm buys fewer actions per turn and needs more turns to reach the same island. Against a 40-60 minute gateway target that is the most serious open number in the game, and this is the knob that moves it. overlays/end-trigger-8.overlay.json is the paired arm; overlays/end-trigger.sweep.json is the full ladder.
unresolved: commonsTake IS DEAN'S VARIANT (09/09/2026), READ ONLY UNDER visitCurrency 'commons' and SHIPPED AT 'harvest', which must stay bit-reproducible. His words: "Your bonus action can be to place 1 card in the centre [and take that board's action], OR take all the cards on one pile (without playing a card). If you take the pile of cards, instead of going into the barn, they go into your HAND. So we remove the rule that a harvest takes the cards from one central card. Effectively we change the bonus action into a draw instead of a harvest." 'bonus' is the unrun variant at overlays/commons-take-to-hand-v1.overlay.json: Harvest never reaches the centre (commonsHarvestMin and commonsHarvestTake have no subject), and a new free bonus move, commonsTake, draws one whole central pile straight to hand instead. See the knob's own description for the full ruling.

⭐ THE BONUS RATE AGAINST DEAN'S BAND, AND IT IS THE FIRST READING OF THE PASS. The bonus should be played on 30% to 60% of turns (Dean, 09/09/2026); outside that band a17 FAILS. Above 60% the bonus is automatic and it is not a decision, which is exactly how the meeple visit failed at the table; below 30% the centre is not worth a card. rules.economy.commonsThreshold and rules.economy.commonsColourMatch are the two dials, both off, and they are off because a cap should be measured for before it is imposed. ⚠️ There is no noise floor on reference-v15, so a band this wide is readable but a delta inside it is not.

⭐ THE FARM BYPASS: DOES THE CENTRE OUT-SUPPLY THE FARM AS A SOURCE OF BARN CARDS? A Harvest may now take a whole central pile that five players have been feeding, which is a barn faucet that needs no building, no threshold and no Grow. If the share of barn cards arriving from the centre beats the share arriving from own buildings, THE BUILDING ENGINE IS DECORATION - the tableau still scores VP, but the route to the island stops running through it. a18-commons-traffic reports the split and it is an OBSERVE with no ruled threshold, because nobody knows what a healthy split looks like. Read it beside the barn glut, which the same faucet could move in either direction.

THE HAND LIMIT OF 7 IS THE SIMULATOR'S BOUND AND NOT A GAME RULE (C7). The table plays with no limit and Dean found that positive; the enumerator cannot cost an end-of-turn discard without a ceiling. So every report header has to say which it is quoting, and no hand number measured here describes the game Dean is playing. The fix is a bot-side discard heuristic in place of the rule, which nobody has designed, and until it exists overlays/hand-limit-*.json measure the instrument as much as the game.

THE ORCHARD DOOR AT DRAW 2 AGAINST DRAW 3, which is the one contested number in the door set. Dean chose 2 on 09/09/2026. A play costs a card, so Draw 2 nets +1 where every other door hands back a whole action, and the L2 prediction is that the Orchard board goes dead. overlays/commons-draw-three.overlay.json is the paired arm and the door mix is the reading. If Orchard collapses at 2 and thrives at 3, the exception the card visit needed has come back under a different argument.

GAME LENGTH IS STILL THE OPEN NUMBER, AND NOBODY HAS TIMED A REAL TABLE. The meeple economy read 2p 30.0 / 3p 26.5 / 4p 25.1 rounds and v31 33.6 / 28.1 / 25.2, against a 40-60 minute target that has never been verified in minutes. The commons buys an action for a card with no supply to run out, so it could go either way. rules.endGame.deliveriesToTrigger is the knob and overlays/end-trigger.sweep.json is the ladder.

THE BARN GLUT IS UNTOUCHED at +0.5 to +1.0 across four arms, and the commons hands it a new faucet (a harvested central pile) and a new drain (a card a turn leaving the hand for the centre). It is the oldest unfixed reading in the project and the wild substitution is still the only thing that has ever moved it.

THE VEGETABLE DOOR COLLAPSED under both previous versions - 18% of door uses under v31, 8% under the meeple economy - and Deliver is the scoring action. The candidate mechanism nobody has tested: Deliver is the one door whose value depends entirely on the BUYER's barn, so making it cheap does not make it usable. Watch whether the central Harvest, which fills a barn without a building, finally gives the Vegetable board something to be worth.

WHETHER INTERACTION IS A PER-TURN OR A PER-GAME QUANTITY, which is the old hook question surviving its own subject. a08-the-hook has NO SUBJECT under the commons - there is no neighbour to visit - and a18-commons-traffic replaces it, so the same choice has to be made again about plays per turn against plays per game before either number can pass or fail anything.

THE MONOCULTURE PULL (v31 risk 3). The Farmstead pays 1 VP per own-suit card built and the Power and Endgame cards cost 2 cards of their own suit; the own-crop build share was 82.6% before and 83.3% after, and it has not been read under either meeple pass or this one. The commons pushes the other way for the first time - any card pays for any board - so this is worth re-reading rather than assuming.

THE INTERFACE IS NOW TWO VERSIONS BEHIND. packages/ui pins itself to overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json and draws the v31 game: a Notice Board per player, a fill bar, a visit assembled by dragging a card. It never grew the meeple loop and it does not have the commons either. ⭐ THE ENCOURAGING HALF: the commons is a SIMPLER interface than either meeple version - five piles in the centre, drag a card onto one - so the debt is bigger and the job is smaller. See the docblock on `data` in packages/ui/src/session/table.ts.

THE 2-SEAT GAME IS STILL THE SEAT COUNT WITH THE LEAST EVIDENCE BEHIND IT. deliveriesToTrigger is flat, the island is half-used at 12 spaces, and the commons removes the one thing 2p was worst at (one rival board to visit) by putting all five boards in the middle. That is the change most likely to read differently at two seats than at four.

⭐ THE COMMONS WITH COINS IS AN ARM AND NOT THE GAME (Dean, 10/09/2026, docs/commons-coins-handoff-2026-09-10-v2.md, rules K1-K15). FOUR LEAVES HERE ARE ITS OFF SWITCHES AND EVERY ONE OF THEM SHIPS OFF: commonsTake stays 'harvest', commonsWildPair false, endgameCoinCost null and farmsteadCoinPower false, with the four farmsteadPower numbers standing ready but read by nothing while farmsteadCoinPower is off. WHAT THE ARM IS: the bonus slot's second option becomes DISCARD EVERY CARD ON ONE CENTRAL PILE TO ITS SUITS' DISCARDS AND TAKE ONE COIN PER CARD (commonsTake 'coins'), no card paid, and Harvest never reaches the centre (K4, reversing C5); the play half is colour-matched with the wild pair built at last (commonsColourMatch true plus commonsWildPair true, which is D5/D7 of the commons pass finally implemented); and the coins have EXACTLY TWO SINKS AND ONE MINT - the Farmstead as a coin-activated suit power taken as your main action (farmsteadCoinPower, K10-K14) and the fifteen Endgame cards priced in coins instead of two own-suit cards (endgameCoinCost, K15). ⛔ COINS WERE DELETED ON 02/09/2026 (v31) AND EVERY EARLIER COIN ECONOMY IN THIS PROJECT DIED OF A SECOND FAUCET OR A PITY RATE, so the one thing that must never be added here is a third use or a second mint: coins score nothing, break no ties, buy no ordinary card, and leftover coins are dead. island.tileRule.coinsPerDelivery stays pinned at 0 and is a tombstone, not a faucet. overlays/commons-coins-v1.overlay.json is the arm and it pins every passenger by name; commons-coins-no-wild-v1 and commons-coins-endgame-cards-v1 are its two paired sub-arms and commons-coins-endgame-price.sweep.json prices the Endgame card at 2, 3 and 4.
